abstract: Let a pure crystalline Galois representation over a number field be unramified away from an odd prime unramified in the field, with distinct residual cyclotomic characters in the same Fontaine–Laffaille interval as its labelled weights. Every cut between the ordered residual exponents then forces a nonzero strict Selmer class whose negative twist is the difference of two exponents across that cut. Purity supplies a characteristic-zero factor meeting both sides even when the original representation is reducible. An oriented residual extension splits at every decomposition group above the prime. Class field theory identifies the strict kernel with a negative-character part of a cyclotomic class-group quotient, and even algebraic $K$-groups give a gcd divisibility criterion across the cuts. For Alpöge’s ordinary period construction, assume the strict cohomological window on the host fixed before prime selection and the fitted automorphic and local comparisons. Both type primes can then be chosen so that, after the moving-inertia projection, marked strings of intermediate length are absent in every cuspidal rank. A Tate twist also excludes purely cyclotomic marked strings of length one when the leading cusp is spherical at every finite place and the fitted weight enclosure holds. Mixed residual constituents, nonspherical length-one parts, other coefficient characteristics, and the joint signed height and spectral rank estimates remain relevant to the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
title: Strict Selmer classes across the weights of an ordinary period
